text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.5% today after oil prices dropped on news that Saudi Arabia has restored crude flows through its Red Sea pipeline to around 3.5 million barrels per day. The recovery of this supply, combined with broader mediation efforts between the U.S. and Iran that could ease Middle East tensions further, eased concerns about tight global oil markets and knocked crude prices down about 18% from their recent highs (U.S. oil at $96.41 versus the world price at $114.89).

The stock is down 11% over two weeks as energy markets shift from supply-crisis mode back toward normalcy. While potential policy wildcards—like a U.S. diesel export ban or major LNG expansions in Canada—remain in the news, the immediate driver today was simpler supply recovery reducing the premium oil companies could command.
